instrument: Fed hikes 25bp at the October 2026 FOMC meeting

catalyst.event: FOMC meeting October 27-28 2026, decision 14:00 ET on the 28th. No SEP at this meeting. Contract resolves on the decision.
catalyst.action: Buy YES at 18c or better. Hold to resolution — the premium is the risk, there is no useful intermediate exit.

thesis: AMENDS the pending 2026-09-02 pitch of this same contract at 28c; what changed is that the September meeting actually hiked and published a SEP, and the price fell to 18c. The arithmetic of the committee own projections sets a floor above the market price: the September SEP puts the end-2026 federal funds rate at a 4.1 median with a central tendency of 4.1-4.4 and a range of 3.9-4.4. Central tendency excludes the three highest and three lowest projections, so a 4.4 upper bound means at least four of eighteen participants project 4.4 — two more 25bp hikes — and with only October 27-28 and December 8-9 left, two hikes is arithmetically impossible without hiking in October. Four of eighteen is 22%, against a market price of 18%.
key_risk: The minutes say most participants saw another increase as appropriate BY YEAR END, which permits waiting for December, and December is the meeting that carries a SEP to justify a path with. Unemployment has already printed 4.2% against the SEP median of 4.1%, which hands the doves a reason to wait. This is a binary that expires worthless 74% of the time on my own estimate, so it is sized at 1% and the premium is the whole loss.
counter_argument: Back-to-back hikes immediately after breaking a three-year pause are rare, and the market at 18c is probably reading Fed guidance toward December that I have not read. Answered on two grounds: first, the trade does not need October to be likely, only to be worth more than 18c, and the committee own dot distribution puts at least 22% of participants on a path that requires it. Second, the minutes record that participants judged inflation risks skewed to the upside and that they had not seen sufficient progress, with staff August total PCE at 3.8% and core at 3.4% against a 2% goal — an upside-skewed committee at nearly double target is not a committee that reliably waits.

Second the target is 5.8 ATR away on a 1.5501 ATR, which is a long way for a swing even though 67.45 is a real 250-day level, and it requires clearing the 63.77 September high en route. counter_argument: The honest case against is that a pullback entry into a breaking-out sector selects for the scenario where the sector thesis is failing — the exact pattern that gave this report a 42% fill rate on pullback entries. Answered by what the level is made of rather than by preference: 58.40 is not a reflex discount off the last print, it is where the 20-day, the 50-day and three consecutive closes agree, and if price breaks it the energy trade is wrong anyway and the 54.60 stop below the 09-29/09-30 lows of 54.76/54.77 is the correct place to find that out.

thesis: AMENDS the pending 2026-10-10 pitch at 245.50. The level was wrong by a hair and the correction matters: 245.50 sits BELOW the September high of 247.10, so it was not actually a breakout trigger — it was inside the range. The trigger moves to 247.50, above both the September high (247.10) and the October high (245.185), which makes the entry a genuine breakout rather than a pullback. Price has built a higher base since: September lows at 220.46 against October lows at 219.10, then eight sessions holding 232.97-241.63 above the 20-day at 234.11, with the 200-day far below at 218.78. Analyst revisions are improving (63.6% bullish, +1.7pp) and the company has beaten in three of the last four quarters by a consistent small margin (+2.7%, -2.1%, +5.5%, +1.8%), which is the profile that does not blow up on a print.
key_risk: Insiders are selling and not buying: zero open-market purchases in six months against $7.57M of net selling. The target at 288.74 is the 250-day high and sits 6.2 ATR above the entry, which is a long way inside a swing window even for a group with a 2.77% ATR. The entry is conditional on a breakout that has not happened — if STLD never closes above 247.10 this idea costs nothing and delivers nothing. Steel demand is construction-levered into a Fed that has started hiking, and the options-implied move could not be checked this run because the Yahoo options endpoint returned 401.
counter_argument: The strongest case against is the insider selling, and it is not answerable — $7.57M net with no offsetting purchases is management telling you something about price, and it is why this is a conviction 3 sized at 2% rather than a core position. The second case against, that the 288.74 target is simply the 250-day high picked to make the ratio work, is answerable: the stop came first, at 231.50 below the 10-07/10-08 low cluster of 232.97/233.265 and below the 20-day, which is 2.42 ATR of risk — the ratio of 2.58 then falls out of a target that is a real level rather than a number chosen to clear the floor.
